title: 家中的陌生人：从指涉性艺术作业到构成性艺术作业

zh: 家中的陌生人：从指涉性艺术作业到构成性艺术作业
en: Strangers at home: from referential to compositional artworking

zh: 克里斯蒂安·尼扬佩塔
en: CHRISTIAN NYAMPETA

zh: 2019年12月初，我正返回我居住的纽约。我从卡萨布兰卡起飞的航班准时降落在肯尼迪机场，但由于我正在把临时签证转为永久签证，目前重新进入美国需要经历国土安全调查局（HSI）的二次审查程序。当然，国土安全部在某种意义上审查所有赴美访客，只不过这种二次处理在一间由武装警卫押送前往的办公室里进行。一进入那间灯火通明的房间，就变成等待批准的事，身边还有别人，他们和我一样相当滑稽地竭力避免目光接触，掩藏尴尬、疲惫与绝望的混合。
en: At the beginning of December 2019 I was returning to New York, where I live. My flight from Casablanca landed on time at JFK Airport, but because I am in the process of changing my temporary visa to a permanent one re-entry into the United States currently involves undergoing a secondary clearance process by Homeland Security Investigations (HSI). Homeland Security of course scrutinize all visitors to the USA in a way, except that this secondary processing takes place in an office to which one is escorted by armed guard. Once in that brightly lit room, it becomes a matter of waiting for approval, alongside others who, like myself, rather comically do everything that they can to avoid eye contact and hide their mix of embarrassment, exhaustion and desperation.

zh: 我已经习惯这种经历，此前经历过多次，但这次不同：我被叫进
间办公室。“克里斯蒂安先生，”一个威严的声音说，“请跟我走这边。”声音的主人身穿便装，但我猜想他右臀处的鼓包是一把隐藏的手枪。我完全沉默地跟着他，越来越深入机场迂回的内部，每一步都让我的焦虑增加，直到我们到达目的地。
en: I was used to this experience, having gone through it a number of times already, but this occasion was different in that I was called into a

office. ‘Mr Christian’, a commanding voice said, ‘please follow me this way.’ The person behind the voice was in civvies, but I assumed the bulge on his right hip was a concealed handgun. I followed him in complete silence deeper and deeper into the circuitous interiors of the airport, each step causing my anxiety to increase, until we reached our destination.

zh: 移民官用力握了握我疲惫的手。他确认了我的全名和出生日期，没有自我介绍，指示我坐在他办公桌对面的一把椅子上。他坐下，把我的护照和移民卡放在旁边，在键盘上敲了几下，但随即放弃电脑，拿起一个笔记本，翻到空白页，告诉我被叫来是为了更好地了解我。我没什么可担心的；只需回答他的
问题，我
很快就能离开。我咕哝着表示同意，在椅子上不安地挪动。
en: The immigration officer firmly shook my tired hand. He confirmed my full name and date of birth, refrained from introducing himself, and instructed me to sit at his desk in a chair opposite his own. He took his own seat, placed my passport and immigration card down next to him, hit a few keys on his keyboard, but then immediately abandoned his computer, picked up a notebook, turned over the page to reveal a blank one and told me that I had been called in so that he could get to know me better. I had nothing to worry about; all I had to do was answer
his questions and I
out of there in no time. I muttered something in acquiescence, shuffling awkwardly in my chair.

zh: 这则轶事是一场演讲的开端；演讲最初被宣布为视听演示，以一组朴素的问题开始：我的名字为什么叫克里斯蒂安？如何建立关于当今生活限度的记忆？如何把有时相互矛盾、尽管都真实的记忆分层？如何把单一的民族与官方记忆同多重个体记忆、集体记忆、也许还有地理的、地质的与生态的记忆调和起来？
en: This anecdote was the beginning of a presentation that was initially announced as an audiovisual presentation commencing with a set of unadorned questions: How come my name is Christian? How to build a memory of present-day limits of living? How to layer the memories that are sometimes contradictory, even though they are all true? How to reconcile the singular national and official memory with the multiple individual, collective memories, and perhaps even the geographical, geological and ecological ones?

zh: 想法是通过一部合作性、开放式的影片《一起思考的人一起跳舞》中的声音与视觉片段来处理这些问题。影片通过“声音社会”结构，以播放列表的形式建构社会生态；播放列表取材于艺术集会、哲学会议、社交聚会、教学集会与灵性对话，在历史断裂、不连续、脱节的连续性及其他此类思考模式所产生的地域与知识之内和之外。确实，《一起思考的人一起跳舞》是艺术家兼图书管理员兰戈阿托·赫拉萨内发起的集体聚会与声音集会的名称，作为“艺术教育另一路线图非洲集群”研讨会的组成部分；该研究项目关于艺术教育史，由四大洲的教育者、艺术家与研究者网络开展，始于苏黎世艺术大学（ZHdK）艺术教育研究所。
en: The idea was to address these questions through sonic and visual fragments from a collaborative and open-ended film,

children: People Who Think Together Dance Together

en: . The film constructs social ecologies through ‘audiosocial’ structures in the form of a playlist that draws from artistic assemblies, philosophical conferences, social gatherings, pedagogical convenings and spiritual conversations, within and beyond spaces and knowledges that come out of historical ruptures, discontinuities, disjointed continuities and other such modes of thinking. Indeed,

is the name of collective parties and sonic gatherings initiated by the artist and librarian Rangoato Hlasane as an integral component of the symposiums of Another Roadmap for Arts Education Africa Cluster, a research project on the history of arts education undertaken within a network of educators, artists and researchers working in four continents, initiated at the Institute for Art Education at Zurich University of the Arts (ZHdK).
**From ‘**

zh: 但正如提及时几乎显得多余，上述公告发布的2020年1月，与我现在写作的2020年5月，看起来和感觉起来都大不相同。
与世界大多数地方一样，纽约的博物馆关闭，所有展示空间也关闭。相反，一些展览、讲座、放映与表演迁移到线上。此前，在当前危机汇聚开始之前，当代艺术
什么这一问题，本来可以通过审视当代艺术

可接触来回答：当代艺术曾是广大公众与观众在正午之前几乎遇不到、也很少在下午六点之后（每周特定日子到晚上九点）遇到的艺术作品。换言之，由画廊与博物馆保存、授权并保护下来的当代艺术，几乎无人与之共同生活。我已经对这类不被共同生活的艺术作品之日常性社会学感到着迷。而如今，为尽量减少病毒传播而全国强制实施的居家令，让我想到自己与那位移民官的个人遭遇。以下是对“不被共同生活的艺术作品”这一悖论如何把艺术工作者塑造成自己家中的陌生人的反思。为此，我回到与HSI移民官的遭遇。
en: But, as it is almost obsolete to mention, the moment of January 2020 in which the above announcement was made looks and feels very different from the month of May 2020 in which I write.

As has been the case in most parts of the world, in New York museums are closed and so are all spaces of display. Instead, some of the exhibitions, talks, screenings and performances have migrated online. Previously, before the onset of the current convergence of crises, the question of
contemporary art is could have been addressed by looking at

contemporary art is accessible: contemporary art had been artworks that wider publics and audiences scarcely encounter before noon and rarely past 6 pm (9 pm on select days of the week). In other words, the contemporary art preserved, mandated and conserved by the gallery and the museum is barely lived with. I was already fascinated by something akin to the sociology of the quotidian of such artwork that is not lived with. And now, with the nationwide mandatory sheltering directives that are currently in effect in order to minimize the spread of the virus, this new restriction of mobility reminds me of my personal encounter with the immigration officer. The following is a reflection on how this paradox of ‘artworks that are not lived with’ gives shape to artworkers as strangers in their own home. In order to do this, I return to my encounter with the HSI immigration officer.

zh: 当我坐在他办公室里、感觉像是一种

时，官员向我解释：“基本上，你被我们的系统标记了，因为你是从马里旅行回来的。”他停顿，直视我。“你做什么工作？你在马里做什么？待了多久？住在哪里？跟谁接触？去过哪些地方？”这连串提问让我有点吃惊，我咕哝说参加了巴马科双年展，展览在马里首都巴马科的多个文化机构举行。我住在友谊酒店，整个旅程由马里文化部长办公室安排，事实上我是应其邀请出行的。我给官员看了新闻稿、邀请函，以及双年展上收到的徽章和手提袋。我甚至拿出了一张萨利夫·凯塔的照片，是我在马里国家博物馆的一场开幕式上拍的。我也拍了总统本人的照片，但我说，我更满意的是给文化部长恩迪亚耶·拉马图拉耶·迪亚洛拍的那张，因为她的开幕演讲令人激动不已。
en: ‘Basically’, the officer explained to me as I sat in what felt like a

in his office, ‘you were flagged up in our system because you are travelling from Mali.’ He paused and looked directly at me. ‘What do you do for work? What were you doing in Mali? How long were you there for? Where did you stay? Who were you in contact with? What places did you visit?’ I was taken a little aback by the rapid questioning and mumbled that I had attended the Bamako Biennale held across a number of cultural institutions in Bamako, the capital of Mali. I had stayed at Hôtel l’Amitié and my entire journey had been organized by the Office of the Malian Minister of Culture on whose invitation I was, in fact, travelling. I showed the officer a press release, my invitation letter, and the badge and tote bag I had received at the Biennale. I even produced a picture of Salif Keita, which I had taken at one of the opening ceremonies at the National Museum of Mali. I had also taken a photograph of the president himself, but, I said, I was more pleased with my picture of N’Diaye Ramatoulaye Diallo, the minister of culture, because I had found her opening speech nothing short of electrifying.

zh: “什么是双年展？”官员问。他让人难以捉摸。我不确定这是不是一个真诚的问题。他还问萨利夫·凯塔是谁，并重复之前的问题：“你做什么工作？”“我是艺术家，”我终于迟疑地回答。“一位视觉艺术家，”我赶紧澄清。我自己也开始质疑这究竟意味着什么，以及那是否真的是我。官员不慌不忙地记了些笔记。他一定感觉到我锐利的目光落在他手上，因为他停下来告诉我，这次面谈——他这样称呼——的目的是让他建立对我的全面档案，以便假设面谈成功，下次我的名字被无意标记时，“系统”会自动驳回我的案子。我随后会被允许进入美国，而无需这种HSI严厉盘问。
en: ‘What is a biennale?’, the officer asked. He was hard to read. I was not sure if this was a genuine question. He also asked who Salif Keita was and repeated his earlier question: ‘What do you do for work?’ ‘I am an artist’, I finally responded, hesitantly. ‘A visual artist’, I quickly clarified. I was myself starting to question what that actually meant and whether that was actually what I was. The officer unhurriedly took some notes. He must have felt my piercing eyes on his hand because he stopped to tell me that the object of the interview, as he called it, was for him to build a comprehensive profile of me, so that, assuming the interview was successful, next time my name was inadvertently flagged, the ‘system’ would automatically dismiss my case. I would then be admitted into the USA without the need for this HSI third-degree processing.

zh: 我暂时放松下来，直到官员再次问道：“什么是艺术？”我又仔细端详他的脸，却无法判断出任何单一情绪。我断定他是极其认真的。我吃了一惊，官员的问题——“什么是艺术？”——变成了“艺术做什么？”我记得，正如艺术家劳伦斯·阿布·哈姆丹会说的，按听者的准备程度说话对我最有利。我的听者很可能对我的热情并不认同，我必须非常注意自己说的话。然而，尽管怀着最好的意图，问题还是自行蒸馏为“艺术作业不做什么？”，从那里，我的头脑又诱使我转向“艺术作业撤销什么？”
en: I momentarily relaxed until the officer asked again: ‘What is art?’ I took another close look at his face but could not determine a single emotion. I concluded he was deadly serious. Startled, the officer’s question – ‘what is art?’ – became ‘what does art do?’ I remembered that it was in my greatest interest to speak at the readiness of my listener, as artist Lawrence Abu Hamdan would say. My listener could very well be unsympathetic to my enthusiasm and I had to be very mindful of what I said. However, despite my best intentions, the question distilled itself into ‘what does artworking not do?’, and from there my mind tricked me into moving to ‘what does artworking undo?’

zh: 当我坐在移民官对面，尽力圆满回答他的问题时，我的头脑在运算一个假设：艺术作品是艺术家行动的索引，艺术家是具有自由能动性的社会人物，能够把自身的感官、行动、运动及其他物质——以及他们所代表者的那些——解释并转化为具有文化价值的作品。由于我处于自我保全模式，我的思维引擎把这个公理倒转过来，艺术作品开始显示艺术工作者
做什么。
en: As I sat opposite the immigration officer trying my best to answer his questions to his satisfaction, my mind was computing a hypothesis that an artwork is an index of the artist’s actions, whereby artists are social figures with free agency, capable of interpreting and transforming their senses, actions, movements and other matter – as well as those of whom they represent – into works of cultural value. As I was in self-preservation mode, my thinking engines inverted this axiom and an artwork started to reveal what the artworker does
do.

zh: 在此，艺术作品似乎显现为艺术工作者“非行动”的储藏库。非行动不是不作为。艺术作业很少是什么都不做；其生产总有能量与劳动的支出。它始终是一种物质现实，尽管有时无形。因此这种非活动确实是能量的支出，而这种能量正在
某物。这是因为艺术作品把自己置于它所从出的背景之前，这一涌现是社会、文化、有时（当它“成功”时）经济的脱离过程。反过来，这种脱离使一件艺术作品区别于其他艺术作品，也区别于一般的“工作”。这种从背景中的涌现本质上是一种指涉。
en: Here, an artwork seemed to appear as a depository of what I saw as the ‘non-actions’ of the artworker. Non-actions are not inactions. Artworking is rarely doing nothing; there is always an expenditure of energy and labour involved in its production. It is always a material reality, though sometimes formless. Thus this non-activity is indeed an expenditure of energy and this energy is

something. This is because an artwork sets itself against the background from which it emerges, this emergence being a process of social, cultural and sometimes, when ‘successful’, economic detachment. In turn, this detachment is what distinguishes an artwork from other artworks, but also from ‘work’ in general. This emergence from the background is essentially a reference.

zh: 我不确定官员是否听懂了我的话，或者，即使听懂了，我也不确定他是否同意。他质疑我的假设也许有道理，因为悖论性地，这源于
给予艺术作品所从出的指涉以前景。事实上，艺术作品
前景；它设立新的前沿，使艺术作品脱离其背景。换言之，艺术作品
其指涉的前景，撤销其“先在性”。
en: I am not sure if the officer understood what I was saying, or, if he did, I am not sure he agreed with me. He might be right to question my hypothesis because, paradoxically, it follows from
the foreground to the reference from which the artwork emerges. In fact, an artwork
the foreground; it sets a new front and it detaches the artwork from its background. In other words, an artwork
the foreground of its reference, its ‘previousness’.

zh: 这时，官员问我出生在哪里。我并不总是欢迎这个问题，恰恰因为，作为艺术工作者，我的出生地有时是我可能努力撤销的“先在性”的一部分，因为人当然不可能既是艺术家又仍拥有国籍……我在心里想，实际上，艺术作品的吸引力、成功与被接受，都在这一张力的解决之中：尽管艺术家有非行动，作品仍涌现并使自己区别于背景，把自己物质化为具有文化价值的作品。我温和地指出，我的出生地写在护照上。
en: By this time, the officer was asking me where I was born. I do not always welcome this question, precisely because, as an artworker, where I was born is sometimes part of my previousness that I may strive to undo, for surely one cannot be an artist and still have a nationality… Effectively, I thought, the attraction to an artwork, its success and its acceptance reside in the resolution of this tension: despite the artist’s non-action, the artwork emerges and distinguishes itself from the background, and materializes itself as work of cultural value. I pointed out, gently, that my place of birth was stated on my passport.

children: 艺术作业与现实的“生成性”抹除
Artworking and the ‘generative’ erasure of reality

zh: 我继续勤勉地回答移民官的问题，但我的头脑已开上自己的失控列车。一件作品通过“雕塑”成为艺术作品。艺术作品的涌现既是对物质的移除，也是赋形，其目的是转化对“现实”的感知。这是一个同样悖论的“生成性”抹除现象。即便在表演、跳舞或绘画时，艺术作业也在移除、亦即
移动现实，通过景观化感知，把一种现实形式塑造成另一种。
en: I continued to diligently answer the immigration officer’s questions, but my mind was on its own runaway train of thought. A work becomes an artwork through ‘sculpting’. The emergence of an artwork is both a removal and a shaping of matter, effected in order to transform the perception of ‘reality’. This is an equally paradoxical phenomenon of ‘generative’ erasure. Even when performing, dancing or painting, artworking
moves reality, shaping one form of reality into another, by landscaping perception.

zh: 此时官员正在检查我（荷兰）护照上的印章。这使我想起“景观”或荷兰语
，它源于对土地的塑造。我想到这种“造景”如何在大多数艺术领域中被观察到：现实被采作待塑造的原材料。人们可以把历史想成现实的来源，把社会想成现实的来源，把技术想成现实的来源，把规训想成现实的来源，把流行文化想成现实的来源，把谱系想成现实的来源，把语言想成现实的来源，等等。
en: By now the officer was examining the stamps in my (Dutch) passport. This made me think of ‘landscape’ or

in Dutch, which originates from shaping the land. I thought about how this ‘scaping’ could be observed in most artistic fields whereby reality is sourced as raw material to be shaped. One can think of history as the source of reality, society as the source of reality, technology as the source of reality, discipline as the source of reality, popular culture as the source of reality, genealogy as the source of reality, language as the source of reality, and so on.

children: 现实的来源及其在艺术作业中的显现
Sources of reality and their manifestation in artworking

zh: 对这些现实来源的反思，指引我走向由这些来源“造景”所产生的艺术形式。例如，我想到某些艺术作品如何以技术作为其历史指涉，并暗示如果这种技术成为社会常态，未来可能是什么样。同样，档案及其内容作为取材于历史的艺术作品而出现。艺术工作者在其中的角色往往包括干预行为、编辑性重排、博物馆学呈现，以及支持或反对原始材料中历史叙述的论辩性或纠正性主张。除了其他明显好处，这种档案互动的能动性还起到赋予委托机构正当性的作用，即便作品对之持批判态度。
en: Reflecting on these sources of reality pointed me to the artistic forms that result from the ‘scaping’ of these sources. For example, I thought how certain artworks take technology as their historical referent and suggest what the future might look like if this technology became the societal norm. Similarly, archives and their contents emerge as artworks that source history. The artworker’s role therein tends to include interventional acts, editorial reordering, museological presentations and polemical or corrective propositions for or against a historical account contained in the source material. Alongside other obvious benefits, the agency of such archival interactions serves to validate the commissioning institution, even where the work is critical of it.

zh: 接着我想到艺术作业机构如何以博物馆的保存律令为模型。当然，这对不出售或收藏艺术作品的机构也成立。我记得在某处读到的一个说法：就“差异性纳入”而言，艺术作业机构总是会从艺术作品的善意——以及对立的敌意——中获益。然后我落到社会参与式艺术作业上，这也是我自己的实践经常被归入的类别。我听见内心耳朵里的低语。社会参与式艺术作业往往通过从社区获取现实来进行，从委托机构扩展街区、网络或集群中社区群体的人力、社会、历史与文化资源中取材。这些互动的成果之前有工作坊：邀请专家主持学习项目，使艺术家与参与者或贡献者受益，有时也使机构受益。从这些工作坊中可能产生艺术作品。它们可能是工作坊的录音、由社区成员主办或包括社区成员的新活动，以及通过某种可转移技能工作坊制作的工艺物品。集体制作的物品可以作为展览重新分配，或在社区中分配给相关利益方。有时艺术作品是“有用的”，例如公共艺术作品：除了象征方面，它们还在委托机构内外具有功能目的。
en: Next I thought about how artworking institutions are modelled after the preservative imperative of the museum. This is, of course, also the case for institutions that do not sell or collect artworks. I remembered an expression I had read somewhere: in terms of ‘differential inclusion’, an artworking institution will always benefit from the benevolence – and the antagonism – of an artwork. I then landed on socially engaged artwork, which is the way my own practice is regularly categorized. I heard whispers in my inner ear. Socially engaged artwork tends to be undertaken through sourcing reality from the community, drawing from the human, social, historical and cultural resources of community groups in the expanded neighbourhood, network or cluster of the commissioning institution. The outcomes of these interactions are preceded by workshops where an expert is invited to lead a programme of learning that benefits the artist and the participants or contributors and sometimes also the institution. From these workshops, artworks may emerge. They might be recordings of the workshops, new events hosted by or including members of the community, as well as craft-based objects produced through some kind of transferable skills workshop. The collectively produced objects could be redistributed as exhibitions, or distributed across the community to the stakeholders involved. At times, the artworks are ‘useful’, as in the case of public artworks, for instance: beyond their symbolic aspect, these also have a functional purpose inside or outside the commissioning institution.

zh: 我继续沉溺于思考：从谱系背景中涌现的艺术作品，如何通过教育的原型发展出来。其中许多被描述为研究型项目、策展研究或艺术研究，其实质与成果都是物质的，即便焦点是一个主题、定理、论文或理论，并可能以学位、奖学金或艺术作业机构的关联职位的形式得到回报。这些活动可以呈现为综述区域、国家或跨国主题的调查展；双年展及其卫星附录；或作为研究展览中的搬演，反之亦然。展出的作品可能包括档案、影片、部分或完整的图书馆，以及作为教学枢纽或工作站的布景或场景。随附的卷册或图录会出版。此处关键的不是作品的独异性，而是每件作品对一个主题、策展课题或立场的论证能力。
en: I continued to indulge in thinking about how artworks that emerge from the background of genealogy are developed through the archetypes of education. Many of them are described as research-based projects, curatorial research or artistic research, and their substance and their outcome are material, even when the focus is a theme, a theorem, a thesis or a theory that may be rewarded in the form of an academic degree, a fellowship or an associate position at an artworking institution. These activities may be presented as survey exhibitions that overview regional, national or transnational thematics; as biennales and their satellite appendixes; or as stagings within research exhibitions and vice versa. The exhibited works may include archives, films, partial or complete libraries and settings or scenes that function as pedagogical hubs or working stations. Accompanying volumes or catalogues are published. What is crucial here is not the singularity of the work but the argumentative ability of each work towards one thematic, curatorial subject or position.

zh: 同样的谱系背景也可以从“身体”范畴中取材，解剖身体、社会身体、文化身体、公共身体、历史身体或政治身体，都作为待重塑的现实来源。对现实感知的重塑在起作用，而取材于身体显现的艺术作品参与了这一重塑。这些作品的生产过程往往涉及“表演”，而这一范畴与艺术概念本身一样狭窄而宽泛。
en: The same genealogical background can be sourced from the categories of the ‘body’, whereby the anatomical body, the social body, the cultural body, the public body, the historical body or the political body all serve as a source of reality to be reshaped. A reshaping of the perception of reality is at play and the artwork that sources the manifestations of the body partakes in this reshaping. The processes through which these artworks are produced tend to involve ‘performance’, which is a category as narrow and as broad as the concept of art itself.

zh: 表演的目标是做什么或达成什么。在金融与管理习语中，performance（业绩）是行动者——例如资产、资源或产品——之属性与特征的指标。例如，销售代理人如果达到或超过销售目标，就表现良好。网站或应用如果吸引读者、下载或使用时长，就表现良好。换言之，业绩与劳动相连，而由于凡有劳动处即有剥削，业绩表明这种剥削如何能被最小化——或最大化。这种剥削的收益有时以薪水、奖金、利润或亏损来表达，但其尺度——尽管任意——是相关行动者或机构表现得多好或多坏。
en: The objective of a performance is to do something or to achieve something. In financial and managerial idioms, performance is an indicator of the properties and the attributes of an actor; for example, an asset, a resource or a product. A sales agent, for instance, performs well if they meet or exceed their sales target. A website or an app performs well if it attracts readership, downloads or airtime. In other words, performance is linked to labour and, because wherever there is labour there is exploitation, performance indicates how such exploitation can be minimized – or maximized. The yield of this exploitation is sometimes expressed through a salary, a bonus, a profit or a loss, but its measure, albeit arbitrary, is how well or how badly the actor or agency in question has performed.

zh: 但

表现如何？我会被允许重新入境吗？也许此时我并不真的在意，继续向官员解释艺术“撤销”什么。表演是一个有力的范畴，用来考察作为非行动储藏库的艺术作品，因为它不同于其他艺术作业范畴——那些范畴植根于艺术家工作室的传统，和／或其通常不对观看公众开放的当代等价工作空间。表演当然可能需要使用工作室来研究、排练和发展，但其交付与体验依赖于观众在场，同时艺术工作者（重新）生产作品——同时劳作。因此，艺术工作者与公众的双重在场才是表演的实际产品；这是前提条件，有时甚至是作品生产背后的目的与动机。表演似乎在说：我存在。这个身体存在。这个某人存在。我的经验以及产生它的存在具有德性、价值、有效性或紧迫性。
en: But how was

performing? Was I going to be allowed back into the country? Maybe I did not really care at this point, continuing to explain what art ‘undoes’ to the officer. Performance is a compelling category for examining an artwork as a depository of non-actions, being unlike other categories of artworking that are rooted in the tradition of an artist studio and/or its contemporary equivalent working spaces that are usually inaccessible to the viewing public. A performance may of course require the use of a studio to research, rehearse and develop the performance, but the delivery and the experience rely on the presence of an audience while the artworkers (re)produce the work – while labouring. The double presence of the artworkers and the public is thus the actual product of a performance; it is a prerequisite, and sometimes even the object and motivation behind the production of the work. A performance seems to say: I exist. This body exists. This somebody exists. There is virtue, value, validity or urgency to my experience and to the existence that produces it.

zh: 即便艺术家通过远程出场基础设施预先录制或现场出现在屏幕上，或者艺术家招募代理人、参与者或合作者代表艺术家施行表演，重要的仍是艺术家——或其所代表者——的在场、传记、存在、问题、身体。表演是身体事务的生产，以及这种身体能够存在的社会与文化条件。这是一个确认身体事务及其生命的过程。表演在展示空间中的文化评价、流通与分配，取决于委托或自主发起活动的公众出席。为此，表演似乎需要公众和一个舞台，表演在此发生、展开、纠正、补偿或处理特定的历史、问题、记忆或未来。此外，“生产”公众与舞台也是表演的目的。机构目标可能是举办活动、工作坊与表演，以生产新政策与新公众。因此，即便表演是越界的，这也有助于为表演艺术家与委托事业或机构积累更多社会地位。
en: Even when an artist appears either pre-recorded or live on a screen via a remote appearance infrastructure, or when the artist enlists deputies, participants or collaborators that carry out the performance on the artist’s behalf, what matters is the presence, the biography, the existence, the problem, the body of the artist or what/who they represent. Performance is the production of body matters, and the social and cultural conditions in which such a body can exist. It is a process of affirmation of the matters of the body and its lives. The cultural valuation, circulation and distribution of performance in spaces of display depend on the public attendance of commissioned or self-initiated events. For this, performance seems to necessitate a public and a stage on which a performance takes place, and unfolds, corrects, redresses or addresses a given history, problem, memory or future. Furthermore, it is the object of a performance to ‘produce’ a public and a stage. It can be an institutional aim to stage events, workshops and performances in order to produce new policies and new publics. As such, even when the performance is transgressive, this serves to accumulate further social standing for the performing artist and the commissioning cause or institution.

zh: 在这个意义上，表演似乎为一切艺术作业形式提供燃料。但艺术作业在表演什么，为什么——为了达成什么？表演的最终目的是什么，它
做什么？换言之，艺术工作者的表演以何种方式塑造和重塑现实？艺术家的在场如何揭示他们所撤销的东西？艺术家的表演以何种方式揭示他们的非行动？艺术家在任何展示空间——家庭、公共或私有——中的在场，都被框定为在中心或边缘的“归属”。实际上，归属是表演的目的。表演以及一般意义上的艺术作业，是确认归属的过程，而争论在于承认什么是中心、什么是边缘。
en: In this sense, performance seems to fuel every form of artworking. But what is artworking performing and why – to achieve what? What is the finality of the performance and what does it

do? In other words, in what way does an artworker’s performance shape and reshape reality? How can the presence of the artist reveal what they have undone? In what ways can an artist’s performance reveal their non-actions? The presence of the artist in any given space of display, be it domestic, public or privately owned, is framed as a ‘belonging’ in the centre or in the margin. In effect, belonging is the object of performance. Performance and artworking in general are a process of affirming belonging, and the contention resides in the recognition of what the centres are and what the margins are.

children: 美的艺术作业与一切艺术作业的金标准
Fine artworking and the gold standard of all artworking

zh: 我接着思考，
（fine art）——至少在英语中——是为艺术而艺术，就艺术作业的最终目的是艺术本身而言；但我也想到，美的艺术这一名称也许是艺术作业的一种特定金融分类。美的艺术甚至可能是这类艺术所代表之阶级的象征性不朽化。换言之，美的艺术自称不受政治困扰，是一种隐蔽的主张：保存它所从出的社会指涉。
en: I went on to think about how

, at least in English, is art for art’s sake, in the sense that the finality of artworking is art itself, but I also thought that the denomination of fine art might be a specific financial categorization of artworking. Fine art might even be the symbolic immortalization of the class that such art represents. In other words, fine art’s claim to be unbothered by the political is a veiled claim to conserve the social reference from which it emerges.

zh: 确实，艺术作业有时假定脱离现实，但（美的）艺术实际上从（艺术）历史中汲取现实，作为它据以塑造自身的首要现实来源，但这一次没有对这样的背景进行去形或撤销。艺术作品也可以对另一件艺术作品提供评论。当然，它也可以对流行文化作品或非美的艺术作品提供评论。这些相互评论有很大价值。例如，一件美的艺术作品可以反对先前历史中美的艺术作品的缺席：艺术作品可以由一个代表性不足的社区成员创作。
en: Indeed, sometimes artworking supposes detachment from reality, but (fine) art, in fact, draws from (art) history as the primary source of reality from which it shapes itself, but this time without unshaping or undoing such background. An artwork may also offer a commentary on another artwork. It can, of course, also offer a commentary on a work from popular culture or a non-fine artwork. There is great merit to these mutual commentaries. For instance, a fine artwork can speak against the absence of fine artworks in previous histories: an artwork can be produced by a member of an under-represented community.

zh: 这种代表性不足意味着收藏不足，而这通常最终归结为终于融入一个迄今拒绝其部分成员的世界。融入可能意味着适应或接受不正义，而这可能意味着那些不正义将继续。无论这种差异性纳入的姿态显得多么含糊，反对蓄意缺席可能是关键而紧迫的，因为一件潜在或实际被博物馆收藏的美的艺术作品，是一切艺术生产的金标准。
en: This under-representation means under-collected and this generally culminates in finally fitting into a world that has thus far rejected some of its members. To fit in may impute adjusting to or accepting injustice, and this could mean that those injustices will continue. However ambiguous this gesture of differential inclusion may appear, speaking against deliberate absences can be crucial and urgent, because a fine artwork, virtually or actually collected by a museum, is the gold standard of all artistic productions.

zh: 这里我想起艺术家兼研究者埃玛·沃卢考-瓦南布瓦的评论：博物馆不应只被理解为一栋“作为一个去看艺术的地方”的建筑；博物馆还应被理解为其“在美的艺术话语场语境中的功能”。这是因为，至少“在西方美的艺术话语中，‘博物馆’实质上起着金标准的作用——价值的担保人。即便你从未去过博物馆，更不用说让你的作品被博物馆收藏，对其存在价值的信念，以及关于其位置与功能的相对共识，意味着艺术话语场中存在的、发生的一切，都以某种方式与它相关——即便这种关系是对立的。”
en: The comments artist and researcher Emma Wolukau-Wanambwa came to mind here: the museum should not only be understood as a building ‘in the sense of a place to go and look at art’; a museum should also be understood in ‘its function within the context of fine art’s discursive field’. This is because, at least ‘within Western fine art discourses, the “museum” essentially functions as a gold standard – a guarantor of value. Even though you may never go to a museum, let alone have your work collected by one, belief in the merits of its existence and a relative consensus regarding its position and function means that pretty much everything that exists and occurs within art’s discursive field somehow happens in relation to it – even when that relation is antagonistic.’

zh: 在这个意义上，“美的”艺术，或现实或观念中的博物馆内的艺术，是评价并因此使所有其他艺术表达不朽的艺术。
en: In that sense ‘fine’ art or the art inside the actual or virtual museums is the art that evaluates and therefore immortalizes all other artistic expressions.

children: 线上与线下的中心与边缘
Online and offline centres and margins

zh: 读者也许会高兴地得知，我顺利重新入境，没有更多麻烦。事实上，我正在纽约的书桌前写这些，周围是一个珍爱的家所能带来的一切舒适。然而，再一次，任何读者都会意识到，2019年12月初的世界与当下2020年5月的时刻大不相同：
en: The reader might be pleased to learn that I was admitted back into the country without further complications. In fact, I am writing this at my desk in New York, surrounded by all the comforts that a cherished home can bring. However, once again, as any reader will be aware, the world of early December 2019 differs greatly from the present moment of May 2020:

zh: Covid-19的爆发迫使所有公共生活骤然停止，并主要从私人住宅中继续进行——对那些负担得起住宅的人而言。我仍然想着与移民官的遭遇，他问我如何谋生。好问题。我回避了这个问题，含糊地解释艺术作品的最终目的确实在于它能被交易。这种交易当然是金融性的，但它定义了跨越博物馆与资助机构轨道系统，以及其间基础设施——包括商业画廊及其慈善家、经销商、艺博会、非营利机构和艺术学校网络——的跨文化交易。“为什么蒙德里安基金会要支持荷兰以外的项目？”官员问我。
en: the outbreak of Covid-19 has forced all public life to grind to an abrupt halt and to proceed mostly from private homes, for those who can afford them. I still think about the encounter with the immigration officer, who asked me how I earn a living. Good question. I avoided the question by explaining vaguely how the finality of an artwork indeed resides in its ability to be transacted. This transaction is of course financial, but it defines the transcultural transactions across the orbital system of the museum and funding institutions alike, and the infrastructures in between, including the commercial gallery, and its network of philanthropists, dealers, art fairs, not-for-profit institutions and art schools. ‘Why would The Mondriaan Fund want to support projects outside the Netherlands?’, the officer asked me.

zh: 在某种意义上，这个问题的答案是对艺术作品所做的双重而同时的归属运动的反思：从边缘到中心，反之亦然。蒙德里安基金会是一种观念形态的博物馆，而任何博物馆都是艺术作业想象中的最终归宿，是有意识地或无意识地担保：保存文化上重要的身体，以承认与（再）分配的形式搬演正义。但在这个金融化、交易性的生态系统中，真正重要的身体是某种
）的身体，一个交易者。
这样，博物馆就是一具活着的石棺，一座
的公共坟墓。在这里重复它们几乎显得多余，但那一刻，安德烈·巴赞的话冲进我的大脑：
en: In a way, the answer to this question is a reflection on the double and simultaneous movements of belonging that an artwork makes, from margins to the centres, and vice versa. The Mondriaan Fund is a virtual type of museum, and any museum is the imagined finality of artworking, the conscious or inadvertent guarantor of keeping the body that matters culturally, of staging justice in the form of recognition and (re)distribution. But in this financialized, transactional ecosystem, the body that really matters is that of
of some sort, a trader.
In this way, the museum is a living sarcophagus, a public sepulchre of
. It is nearly obsolete to repeat them here, but at that moment the words of André Bazin came rushing through my brain:

zh: 在绘画与雕塑的起源处，存在一种木乃伊情结。古埃及宗教旨在对抗死亡，认为生存取决于肉体的持续存在。因此，通过提供对时间流逝的防御，它满足了人类一种基本的心理需要，因为死亡不过是时间的胜利。人为地保存他的身体外观，就是把它从时间之流中夺走，可以说，把它整齐地收进生命的货舱。因此，面对死亡的现实，通过保存血肉与骨骼来维持外观，是很自然的。
en: at the origin of painting and sculpture there lies a mummy complex.  The religion of ancient Egypt, aimed against death, saw survival as  depending on the continued existence of the corporeal body. Thus,  by providing a defence against the passage of time it satisfied a basic  psychological need in man, for death is but the victory of time. To preserve, artificially, his bodily appearance is to snatch it from the  flow of time, to stow it away neatly, so to speak, in the hold of life.  It was natural, therefore, to keep up appearances in the face of the  reality of death by preserving flesh and bone.

children: 艺术作业的普遍可变性

zh: 事实上，为了让移民官相信我不是“坏人”，我告诉他，我在巴马科双年展获得了欧盟艺术奖。这让我想到一般的艺术家奖项公告，它们往往附有评奖委员会成员的简短引语，他们专注于这个问题：艺术家以何种方式“保存”同时“推进”了其知识领域？此处的假设是，获奖作品由一种从既定、可核实、可量化的现象中取材的现实塑造而成，但以新颖而独特的方式，反映了作品生产的时间、空间、文化、社会与历史时刻。换言之，作品在许多方面必须与艺术史中既有作品相似，但新作品也必须在一个或多个重要方面可区分。如果是这样，那么现实塑造便通过
现实来进行。
en: In fact, in order to convince the immigration officer that I was not ‘a bad guy’, I told him that I had received the European Union Art Prize at the Bamako Biennale. This made me think of the announcements of artist prizes in general, which tend to be accompanied by brief quotations from the awarding jury panel members, who preoccupy themselves with this question: in what way has the artist ‘preserved’ and at the same time ‘advanced’ their field of knowledge? The assumption here is that the winning artwork is shaped from a reality sourced from a given, verifiable and quantifiable phenomenon, but in a novel and distinct way that reflects the time, space, culture, society and historical moment in which the artwork is produced. In other words, the artwork has to be similar in many respects to the existing artworks from art history, but the new artwork also has to be distinguishable in one or more significant ways. If this is the case, then the shaping of reality proceeds by way of
reality.

zh: 在与移民官遭遇期间，我的头脑确实毫不留情，悖论不断堆积，源于艺术作业的律令：不仅保存文化或现实，还要把这个必死的、短暂性的现实转化为某种不死而不可动摇的东西。艺术作业不仅是“我存在”的表演，尤其是“我将存在”的表演。悖论性地，美的艺术作业还宣告“我一直存在”。艺术作业这种想象性的先在，把个体的“我”转化为普遍的“我”，转化为一种建立普遍变量的主体性。确立艺术作业的这种普遍可变性，旨在转化并保存主体、文化与现实，使其延续超出自身物理存在与显现的范围。不可避免地，这种通过在未来再现文化来保存文化的需要，必然会与关于过去、现在因而关于现实未来应当如何的对立愿景发生冲突。
en: During my encounter with the immigration officer, my mind really was unsparing, and paradoxes piled up, born of artworking’s imperative to not only preserve culture or reality, but also transform this mortal and transitory reality into something immortal and intransigent. Artworking is not only the performance of ‘I exist’, but especially of ‘I shall exist’. Paradoxically, fine artworking also proclaims ‘I have always existed’. This imagined pre-existence of artworking transforms the individual ‘I’ into a universal ‘I’, into a subjecthood that institutes a universal variable. The institution of this universal variability of artworking aims at transforming and preserving subjects, cultures and realities beyond their physical existence and manifestations. Inevitably, this need to preserve culture by representing it in the future is bound to clash with opposing visions of what the past, the present and therefore the future of reality should be.

zh: 如果这种现实采样的目的是生产一个普遍变量，那么同一种现实采样也可能生产文化、社会与政治边缘：艺术家的本性就是把他们的现实感知为边缘的，即便他们本人就是中心或代表中心。奖项、奖励乃至委托，都是这种矛盾的例子：中心被感知为边缘。我觉得，在博物馆关闭的这一刻，这一悖论只会加剧。
en: If the object of such sampling of reality is to produce a universal variable, this same sampling of reality can also produce cultural, social and political margins: it is the nature of artists to perceive their reality as marginal, even where they themselves are or represent the centre. A prize, an award or even a commission is an example of such contradiction, whereby the centre is perceived as the margin. I felt that this paradox only became heightened at this moment of the museum closures.

children: 从指涉性到构成性艺术作业？

zh: “社会生态／呈现灾难”是我本应在伦敦ICA“思考艺术”会议上参与的专题小组标题。我不确定我在这里是否处理了这个主题，但我了解到，尽管悖论本身不是问题，我仍不得不下结论：当前的物理隔离状况迫使博物馆重新思考自己身体的显而易见性。实际上，由于目前不可能与构成博物馆固有纪念实践的大多数物质实体发生身体接近，艺术机构纷纷把内容数字化，在正常开放时间之外呈现，其方式与艺术家工作和运作的方式大体相同。计算机与互联网显然相当物质，但其物质方式不同于给绘画和雕塑赋形的结构——艺术作业的祖灵。但在这个过程中，博物馆的收藏越多，其线上在场就越缺乏说服力：机构越具制度性，就越受一种原则性软弱的折磨，无法有意义地回应当下的紧迫性。这种尴尬的无能也许可以由它们“保存”而非干预的律令来解释。在某种意义上，这一目标也有助于解释艺术作业为何生产家中的陌生人：用艺术家兼理论家科乔·埃顺一封电子邮件的话说，这是因为灾难——当前情形下是一场大流行病——同时夸大了所有反保守、超保守与后保守的倾向。
en: ’Social Ecologies/Presenting Catastrophe’ is the title of the panel to which I would have contributed at the ‘Thinking Art’ conference at the ICA in London. I am not sure if I have addressed this theme here, but I have learnt that, although paradoxes are not problems as such, I am compelled to conclude that the current situation of physical distancing has forced the museum to rethink the obviousness of its own body. In effect, since bodily proximity to most of the material substances that constitute the memorial practice inherent to the museum is currently impossible, art institutions have rushed to render their content digitally, beyond their normal opening hours, in much the same way that artists work and operate. Computers and the Internet are obviously quite material, but differently so from the structures that give shape to painting and sculpture – the ancestral ghosts of artworking. But in this process, the more the museum has a collection, the more unconvincing their online presence has become: the more institutional an institution, the more it suffers from a principled infirmity to respond meaningfully to the urgency. This awkward illiteracy might be explained by their mandate to ‘conserve’, as opposed to intervene. In a way, this objective could also help to explain why artworking produces strangers at home: it is, to paraphrase an email from artist and theorist Kodwo Eshun, because a catastrophe – a pandemic, in the current case – exaggerates all anti-conservative, hyperconservative and post-conservative tendencies at the same time.

zh: 以结论的面貌，回到我故意不加质疑、不加问题化地谈论的“现实”是有意义的，因为篇幅有限。用哲学家兼教育家埃马纽埃尔·巴尼韦西泽的话说，这是一种状况，其当下的历史已经驶向一个由知识与数字技术控制所驱动的未来航程，这种控制由容纳政治威权主义的极权资本主义强制执行并主导。这个未来远非可预测，它不稳定、不确定。它孕育着多重危机与致命威胁、野蛮、敌意，正如多项关闭边境的决定、退入民族主义例外论，以及持续存在的各种话语所示——这些话语由一种挥之不去的诱惑所塑造：把同类人类中的某些阶层置于死地，这些阶层的成员仍被视为低劣，可被转化为“科学”进步与权力确认的豚鼠。除了对数字革命的庆祝，面对行星性的病毒威胁，当下表现为“人类危机——人类未能设法构成自身的人性，因此，是地球仍无法成为一个世界的危机，也是人类仍无法完成其人性的危机”。
这场危机对身体、感觉、情感、智力等等构成挑战。尤其，它挑战教育、再现与保存机构作为知识及关系之生产与传播空间的角色。挑战在于从一切生命形式所实践的知识中汲取，重建新的想象空间，走向一种能够毫不含糊地把握所有人类——事实上也包括所有非人类，以及非人类的人类——共属于一种共同生活的新思想。如此，艺术作业就可以从异化的指涉模式转向一种构成性实践，作为一场在共同脆弱性面前提高所有人责任感的运动。
en: In the guise of a conclusion, it makes sense to return to the ‘reality’ about which I have deliberately spoken without questioning or problematizing it, because of the lack of space. In the words of philosopher and educator Emmanuel Banywesize, it is a condition whose present history has embarked on a future course driven by the control of knowledge and digital technologies, enforced and dominated by a totalitarian capitalism which accommodates political authoritarianisms. Far from being predictable, this future is unstable and uncertain. It harbours multiple crises and deadly threats, barbarities, enmities, as shown by the multiple decisions to close borders, by the withdrawal into nationalistic exceptionalisms, and by the persistence of discourses informed by the enduring temptation to inflict death on layers of fellow humans whose members are still perceived as inferior and transformable into guinea pigs for ‘scientific’ progress and the affirmation of power. Beyond the celebration of the digital revolution, and in the face of planetary viral threats, the present manifests itself in ‘the crisis of humanity which cannot manage to constitute its own humanity, and therefore, the crisis of the globe still incapable of becoming a world, and the crisis of humans still unable to accomplish their humanity’.

This crisis constitutes a challenge to bodies, feelings, emotions, intelligence and more. In particular, it challenges the educational, representational and conservational institution as a space for the production and transmission of knowledge and relations. The challenge consists in rebuilding new spaces for the imaginary, drawing from the knowledge practised by all forms of life, toward a new thought capable of apprehending, unambiguously, the co-belonging of all humans – and in fact also all non-humans, and the non-human humans – to a common life. In so doing, artworking could move from the estranging referential mode to a compositional praxis, as a movement that heightens the responsibility of all, in the face of a shared vulnerability.

zh: 我原为2020年2月底伦敦CRMEP—ICA“思考艺术”会议准备了这篇演讲。然而，预料到为应对持续的Covid-19大流行而即将实施的全球封锁（写作时这些措施已生效），我不得不取消行程，未能出席会议。
en: I had prepared this presentation as an address to the CRMEP–ICA

conference in London at the end of February 2020. However, I had to cancel my travel in anticipation of the global lockdowns now in effect in response to the ongoing Covid-19 pandemic, and did not attend the conference.
